## The roadmap heartbeat joins the routine standard (#72)

The roadmap report routine, which every autonomous run creates, still told the setup thread to bind it to the
coordinator's session first. That is the persistent-session pattern `routines/README.md` rules out: on an adopting
project an hourly routine bound to the coordinator re-read about 145k tokens per fire (~$1.70, ~$40 a day around the
clock), and older project prompts built on it wrote every report to an external dashboard.

- New `routines/roadmap-heartbeat.md`, listed in `routines/README.md` and WORKFLOW §13 and checked by the release
  gate. It runs in a **fresh session on every fire**, never bound to the coordinator's or any other session; it reads
  the run's state (`state.json`, roadmap, startable set, pull requests and checks, `owner-word` issues, new issues in
  issue mode, silent threads), wakes the coordinator with one message of facts and ends. The coordinator posts the
  report and acts.
- Hard rules: never release, tag, publish or deploy; change nothing; write to no dashboard, artifact or external
  store; never disable or edit itself; rely on the repository and the forge, not memory.
- It exists only while work runs: the coordinator creates it at the start of a run (`<PROJECT> · Roadmap heartbeat`,
  cron from `wt_config.py --report-cron`) and deletes it at the end, on "stop"/"pause", or when a heartbeat reports
  the run is over. A project in issue mode with a standing queue may keep it.
- `skills/softure-worktree-manager/references/report-routine.md` now only points at the new file; the managed block
  (Roadmap reports), `softure-worktree-manager` and WORKFLOW §8.5 name it. The release gate fails on any file that
  binds a routine to the coordinator's session.

Adopting projects: a run in flight keeps its current report routine until it ends; the next run creates the
heartbeat. A project with a standing report routine replaces it: delete the old one, then let the coordinator create
`<PROJECT> · Roadmap heartbeat` as `routines/roadmap-heartbeat.md` describes.
